title: Temporally Multimode Ion-Ion Entanglement Over 1.2 Kilometer Fibers
authors: Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, And L.-M. Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, and L.-M. Duan

Quantum networks and quantum repeaters represent the promising avenues for building large-scale quantum information systems, serving as foundational infrastructure for distributed quantum computing, long-distance quantum communication, and networked quantum sensing. A critical step in realizing a fu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020803] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of temporally multiplexed ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km fiber, a key step toward quantum repeaters.
motivation: Building large-scale quantum networks requires long-distance entanglement distribution; ion traps are promising but face challenges in extending entanglement over fiber.
method: Trapped ytterbium ions generate entanglement via a photonic interface; temporal multiplexing is used to enhance entanglement generation rate over 1.2 km of optical fiber.
result: Achieved ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km fiber with high fidelity and rate, demonstrating temporal multiplexing as a viable technique.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum repeaters by showing that temporally multiplexed ion-photon interfaces can distribute entanglement over kilometer-scale distances.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and generalized probabilistic theories to classify quantum vs classical behavior.
result: They demonstrate that many standard signatures of quantumness are recovered, and that certain processes long considered classical actually exhibit intrinsic quantum properties.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Adiabatic Preparation Of Thermal States And Entropy-noise Relation On Noisy Quantum Computers
authors: Etienne Granet
Henrik Dreyer
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes an adiabatic protocol to prepare thermal states on noisy quantum computers and derives an entropy-noise relation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but current methods are limited by noise and hardware constraints.
method: The authors design an adiabatic state preparation protocol that leverages the system's natural noise to drive the system towards a thermal state, and they analyze the entropy production as a function of noise parameters.
result: They demonstrate that the protocol can prepare thermal states with high fidelity on current noisy quantum devices, and they establish a quantitative relation between entropy production and noise strength.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for thermal state preparation on near-term quantum computers and offers insights into the interplay between noise and thermodynamics.

title: A Resource- And Computationally-efficient Protocol For Multipartite Entanglement Distribution In Bell-pair Networks
authors: S. Siddardha Chelluri
Sumeet Khatri
Peter van Loock
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 July 2026;
tldr: A resource- and computationally-efficient protocol for distributing multipartite entanglement in Bell-pair networks.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks but existing protocols are resource-intensive; this work aims to reduce overhead.
method: The authors propose a protocol that leverages Bell-pair networks and efficient entanglement swapping to generate multipartite states with minimal qubit and time resources.
result: The protocol achieves significant reductions in required Bell pairs and computational steps compared to prior schemes, while maintaining high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable approach for multipartite entanglement distribution, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Universal Nested Quantum Switch
authors: Jorge Miguel-Ramiro
Maria Flors Mor-Ruiz
Wolfgang Dür
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: A universal nested quantum switch that enables simultaneous routing of multiple quantum information streams through a single device, enhancing quantum network efficiency.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient routing of quantum information, but existing switches are limited to single-stream or simple multi-stream operations. A universal switch that can handle arbitrary nested entanglement swapping is needed.
method: The authors propose a nested quantum switch architecture that uses multiple layers of entanglement swapping and Bell measurements to route quantum states between arbitrary pairs of input and output ports, supporting simultaneous connections.
result: The switch achieves universal routing with polynomial resource scaling and maintains high fidelity, enabling parallel quantum communication channels without crosstalk.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable and practical component for future quantum networks, significantly advancing the capability for multi-party quantum communication.

title: Quantum Geometric Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation For Nonlinear Transport
authors: Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, and Jian Wang

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem connects equilibrium noise to linear response and forms a cornerstone of statistical and quantum physics, yet its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation linking dc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026301] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation for nonlinear quantum transport, linking dc noise to geometric curvature.
motivation: Extend the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to geometry-driven nonlinear transport, which is unexplored.
method: Derives a relation connecting dc noise to the quantum geometric tensor using scattering theory and nonequilibrium Green's functions.
result: A geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation valid for nonlinear transport in quantum systems.
conclusion: Provides a fundamental link between quantum geometry and transport noise, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: High-Temperature Fermionic Gibbs States Are Mixtures Of Gaussian States
authors: Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, And Jiaqing Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, and Jiaqing Jiang

Efficient simulation of a quantum system generally relies on structural properties of the quantum state. Motivated by the recent results by Bakshi et al. on the sudden death of entanglement in high-temperature Gibbs states of quantum spin systems, we study the high-temperature Gibbs states of bounde…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that high-temperature Gibbs states of fermionic systems are mixtures of Gaussian states, enabling efficient classical simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum Gibbs states at high temperature is important for understanding many-body physics, but generic states are hard to simulate; structural properties like Gaussianity can enable efficient algorithms.
method: The authors use cluster expansion techniques and properties of fermionic Gaussian states to show that the Gibbs state can be expressed as a convex combination of Gaussian states above a certain temperature threshold.
result: They establish a rigorous bound on the temperature above which the Gibbs state is a mixture of Gaussian states, and demonstrate that this implies efficient classical simulation via Monte Carlo methods.
conclusion: High-temperature fermionic Gibbs states are classically simulable, extending recent results on entanglement sudden death to fermionic systems and providing a new structural insight for quantum many-body physics.

title: Noise-Resilient Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Sensing Via Indefinite-Causal-Order Error Correction
authors: Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, and Guihua Zeng

Quantum resources can, in principle, enable Heisenberg-limited sensing, yet no-go theorems imply that Heisenberg-limited scaling is generically unattainable in realistic noisy devices. While quantum error correction (QEC) can suppress noise, its use in quantum sensing is constrained by stringent req…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum sensing protocol that uses indefinite causal order (ICO) to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling even in the presence of noise, circumventing no-go theorems.
motivation: Heisenberg-limited quantum sensing is fundamentally limited by noise, and standard quantum error correction imposes stringent requirements that are often impractical. The authors aim to achieve noise-resilient Heisenberg-limited sensing without these constraints.
method: The protocol employs a quantum switch to create an indefinite causal order of two noisy sensing channels, effectively implementing a noise-correcting operation that protects the sensing signal without active error correction.
result: The ICO-based protocol achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling for frequency estimation under various noise models, including dephasing and amplitude damping, with a scaling factor that matches the ideal noiseless case.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order provides a practical resource for noise-resilient quantum sensing, offering a new approach to overcome fundamental limitations in metrology.

title: Metacavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), And Tian Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), and Tian Jiang (江天)

Cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED) harnesses light-matter interactions to produce nonclassical light states. However, a fundamental challenge lies in simultaneously achieving Purcell enhancement and tailored wave front control within a single cavity, due to conflicting resonator requirements. Her…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a metacavity that simultaneously achieves Purcell enhancement and wavefront control for generating nonclassical light states.
motivation: Cavity QED faces a fundamental trade-off between Purcell enhancement and wavefront control; the authors aim to overcome this by designing a metacavity that integrates both functionalities.
method: They design a metacavity using a photonic crystal cavity with a metasurface, enabling simultaneous control of the local density of optical states and the far-field emission pattern.
result: The metacavity achieves a Purcell factor of 10 and directional emission with a divergence angle of 5°, producing single-photon states with high purity.
conclusion: The metacavity approach resolves the conflict between Purcell enhancement and wavefront control, offering a new platform for quantum light sources and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Characterizing Entanglement Shareability And Distribution In $N$-partite Systems
authors: Hui Li, Ting Gao, And Fengli Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Li, Ting Gao, and Fengli Yan

Exploring the shareability and distribution of entanglement possesses fundamental significance in quantum information tasks. In this paper we demonstrate that the square of bipartite entanglement measures [MATH]-concurrence, which is the generalization of concurrence, follows a set of hierarchica…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012204] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes entanglement shareability and distribution in N-partite systems using squared bipartite entanglement measures, establishing hierarchical monogamy inequalities.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement can be shared among multiple parties is fundamental for quantum information tasks, but a unified framework for N-partite systems is lacking.
method: The authors generalize the concept of concurrence to squared bipartite entanglement measures and derive a set of hierarchical monogamy inequalities that constrain the distribution of entanglement across partitions.
result: They prove that the squared bipartite entanglement measures satisfy monogamy inequalities for arbitrary N-partite states, providing tight bounds on entanglement shareability.
conclusion: The hierarchical monogamy relations offer a powerful tool for characterizing multipartite entanglement and have implications for quantum cryptography and network protocols.

title: Information Causality Beyond The Random-access-code Model
authors: Baichu Yu And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Baichu Yu and Valerio Scarani

Information causality (IC) was one of the first principles invoked to bound a set of quantum correlations. For some families of correlations, this principle recovers exactly the boundary of the quantum set; for others, there is still a gap. We close some of these gaps using a quantifier for IC based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012202] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the principle of information causality beyond the random-access-code model to better bound quantum correlations.
motivation: Information causality is a physical principle that aims to characterize quantum correlations, but existing formulations leave gaps for certain families of correlations.
method: The authors introduce a new quantifier for information causality based on a more general communication task, going beyond the standard random-access-code model.
result: The new quantifier closes some of the gaps, providing tighter bounds on the set of quantum correlations.
conclusion: Information causality remains a powerful principle for understanding quantum nonlocality, and the generalized framework improves its predictive power.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to characterize the fundamental limitations of Lindblad master equations in simultaneously capturing populations and coherences.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations; the authors aim to systematically understand and quantify these limitations.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a semidefinite program (SDP) to find the best possible Lindblad equation approximation for a given open quantum system dynamics.
result: They derive rigorous bounds on the accuracy of Lindblad equations, showing that certain features of the dynamics cannot be captured by any Markovian master equation.
conclusion: The work provides a powerful tool for assessing the validity of Markovian approximations and highlights the need for non-Markovian treatments in certain regimes.

title: Markovian Heat Engine Boosted By Quantum Coherence
authors: Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, and John H. Reina

We evaluate the role of quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource in a noisy, Markovian, one-qubit heat engine. By consuming the coherence of noisy quantum states, we demonstrate that the engine can surpass the classical efficiency limit when operating according to a quantum Otto cycle. The engi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012424] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: A Markovian one-qubit heat engine can surpass the classical Otto efficiency limit by consuming quantum coherence.
motivation: To investigate whether quantum coherence can serve as a thermodynamic resource to enhance the performance of a quantum heat engine beyond classical limits.
method: The authors model a one-qubit Otto cycle with noisy Markovian dynamics and quantify the role of coherence in the working medium's state.
result: The engine's efficiency exceeds the classical Carnot-like bound when coherence is present, demonstrating coherence as a useful resource.
conclusion: Quantum coherence can boost the efficiency of a Markovian heat engine, highlighting the interplay between quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even with unlimited resources.
motivation: Entanglement is crucial for quantum technologies but is fragile; local state discrimination typically destroys it. The authors aim to reconcile these two aspects.
method: They analyze sequential local discrimination of two orthogonal bipartite states, proving that entanglement can be preserved across multiple rounds of discrimination.
result: They demonstrate that entanglement can be sustained unboundedly, contradicting the intuition that local discrimination always degrades entanglement.
conclusion: Sequential local discrimination protocols can be designed to preserve entanglement, offering new insights for quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Detection Of Quantum Entanglement Across The Event Horizon
authors: Patryk Michalski And Andrzej Dragan
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Michalski and Andrzej Dragan

We investigate the problem of distinguishing between separable and entangled states of two quantum wave packets, one of which falls into a black hole. Intuitively, one might expect the two scenarios to be indistinguishable, since the information carried by one wave packet is hidden beyond the event …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012420] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the detection of quantum entanglement across a black hole event horizon, showing that entanglement can be detected despite one wave packet falling into the black hole.
motivation: Understanding whether quantum entanglement can be detected across an event horizon is fundamental for reconciling quantum mechanics and general relativity, and has implications for black hole information paradox.
method: The authors analyze two quantum wave packets, one falling into a black hole, and use quantum information measures to distinguish separable from entangled states, considering the effects of the event horizon.
result: They find that entanglement can be detected across the event horizon, and the detection is possible even when one wave packet is hidden beyond the horizon.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can survive across an event horizon, providing insights into the nature of black holes and quantum information.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for distilling quantum resource states using stabilizer channels, unifying and extending previous distillation protocols.
motivation: High-quality resource states like maximally entangled or private states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography, but are degraded by noise. Distillation protocols are needed to recover them, and a unified framework can improve understanding and efficiency.
method: The authors introduce stabilizer channels as a class of operations that can be used for distillation, and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for distillability. They apply this framework to various resource states, including entangled and private states.
result: They show that stabilizer channels can achieve optimal distillation rates for certain classes of states, and provide explicit protocols that outperform existing methods. The framework also reveals connections between different resource theories.
conclusion: Stabilizer channels offer a powerful and unifying approach to resource state distillation, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that daemonic advantage can be harnessed to charge a quantum battery using a single auxiliary charger, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and standard ergotropy.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising for energy storage, but their charging efficiency is limited. The daemonic gap represents the difference between maximum extractable work with and without quantum information, and bridging this gap could enhance battery performance.
method: The authors consider a protocol where a quantum battery is time-evolved collectively with an auxiliary charger, then energy is extracted by tracing out the charger. They define and analyze the minimum daemonic ergotropy and compare it to the maximum standard ergotropy.
result: They show that daemonic advantage can be achieved, effectively bridging the daemonic gap, and that this advantage can be used to charge multimode batteries via a single auxiliary system.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to enhance quantum battery charging using quantum information, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and energy storage.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws that enhance charging power in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries can surpass classical energy storage limits using collective quantum effects, but the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling in superabsorption is not fully understood.
method: The authors study an N-qubit cavity-coupled quantum battery governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving finite-size scaling laws and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption power scales superlinearly with N, with entanglement playing a key role, and derive scaling exponents that depend on the model parameters.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of quantum battery charging dynamics and highlight the importance of entanglement for achieving quantum advantage in energy storage.

title: Impact Of Multimode Sources On Ensemble-based Quantum Repeaters
authors: Emil R. Hellebek And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Emil R. Hellebek and Anders S. Sørensen

Long-distance entanglement generation at a high rate is a major quantum technological goal yet to be fully realized, with the promise of many interesting applications, such as secure quantum computing on remote servers and quantum cryptography. One possible implementation is using a variant of the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033026] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of multimode sources on the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, showing that multimode operation can significantly improve entanglement generation rates.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation. Multimode sources offer a potential advantage, but their impact on ensemble-based repeaters had not been systematically studied.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for ensemble-based quantum repeaters using multimode sources, considering realistic noise and loss. They derive analytical expressions for the entanglement generation rate and fidelity, and compare with single-mode sources.
result: Multimode sources can increase the entanglement generation rate by orders of magnitude compared to single-mode sources, while maintaining high fidelity. The improvement is most pronounced in the presence of high loss and noise.
conclusion: Multimode sources are a promising approach to enhance the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, bringing long-distance quantum communication closer to practical realization.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores the vast landscape of quantum advantage across multiple domains, revealing a richer and more nuanced picture than commonly appreciated.
motivation: To systematically characterize and understand the diverse forms of quantum advantage beyond the standard computational speedup, including in communication, sensing, and thermodynamics.
method: The authors provide a conceptual review and classification of different types of quantum advantage, drawing on examples from quantum algorithms, communication protocols, and thermodynamic tasks.
result: They identify a wide spectrum of quantum advantages, ranging from exponential speedups to more modest but practically relevant improvements, and highlight the role of resources like entanglement and coherence.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is not a single phenomenon but a multifaceted concept; understanding its full scope is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity of tin-vacancy centers in diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Coupling individual tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities and measuring coherent cooperativity via optical spectroscopy and photon statistics.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, indicating strong coupling and low decoherence, paving the way for deterministic entanglement.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building scalable quantum repeaters and network nodes due to its high efficiency and low noise.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate and stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement generation in large spin ensembles is challenging due to decoherence and noise; the authors aim to turn cavity dissipation into a resource for stabilizing multipartite entanglement.
method: They propose a cavity-mediated dissipative protocol where spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity mode, and by controlling the cavity dissipation, they engineer steady-state entanglement with reconfigurable structure.
result: The protocol produces robust, scalable entanglement among many ensembles, with applications in quantum sensing (e.g., enhanced metrology) and simulation of topological many-body states.
conclusion: Dissipative entanglement engineering offers a practical route to large-scale entangled states for quantum technologies, leveraging noise rather than fighting it.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors; passive methods could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors design a bosonic code that corrects photon loss errors using continuous drives without active measurements, and experimentally demonstrate it in a superconducting cavity.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, meaning the error-corrected qubit lives longer than the best unprotected qubit in the same system.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can outperform active schemes in certain regimes, offering a new path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information survives in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical models.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, in contrast to the power-law decay without recording. This reveals a new phase of information preservation.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes provides a practical strategy to protect fragile quantum information, improving the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for efficient photon extraction with neutral atoms.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional approaches and providing new insights.

title: Towards Unconditional Uncloneable Encryption
authors: Pierre Botteron, Anne Broadbent, Eric Culf, Ion Nechita, Clément Pellegrini, And Denis Rochette
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2157 (2026).

Uncloneable encryption is a cryptographic primitive which encrypts a classical message into a quantum ciphertext, such that two quantum adversaries are limited in their capacity of being able to simultaneously decrypt, given the key and quantum side-information produced from the ciphertext. Since its initial proposal and scheme in the random oracle model by Broadbent and Lord [TQC 2020], uncloneable encryption has developed into an important primitive at the foundation of quantum uncloneability for cryptographic primitives. Despite sustained efforts, however, the question of unconditional uncloneable encryption (and in particular of the simplest case, called an uncloneable bit) has remained elusive. Here, we propose a candidate for the unconditional uncloneable bit problem, and provide strong evidence that the adversary's success probability in the related security game converges quadratically as [MATH], where [MATH] represents the number of keys and [MATH] is trivially achievable. We prove this bound's validity for [MATH] ranging from [MATH] to [MATH] and demonstrate the validity up to [MATH] using computations based on the NPA hierarchy. We furthemore provide compelling heuristic evidence towards the general case. In addition, we prove an asymptotic upper bound of [MATH] and give a numerical upper bound of [MATH], which to our knowledge is the best-known value in the unconditional model.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a candidate for unconditional uncloneable encryption and provides strong evidence for its security.
motivation: Uncloneable encryption is a fundamental primitive in quantum cryptography, but unconditional security (without random oracles) has remained elusive.
method: The authors propose a scheme for uncloneable bit encryption and analyze its security using the NPA hierarchy and other techniques, proving bounds on the adversary's success probability.
result: They prove a quadratic convergence bound for the adversary's success probability for a range of key sizes, and provide numerical evidence for larger key sizes, achieving the best-known upper bound in the unconditional model.
conclusion: The work provides strong evidence that unconditional uncloneable encryption is achievable, advancing the foundations of quantum uncloneability.

title: Entanglement In The Dicke Subspace
authors: Aabhas Gulati, Ion Nechita, And Clément Pellegrini
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2150 (2026).

We provide a complete mathematical theory for the entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states. These quantum states form an important subclass of bosonic states arising in the study of indistinguishable particles. We introduce a tensor-based parametrization where the diagonal entries of these states are encoded as a symmetric tensor, enabling a direct translation between entanglement properties and well-studied convex cones of tensors. Our results bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and the theory of completely positive and copositive tensors. This dictionary maps separability to completely positive tensors, the PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors. We establish that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension [MATH] and [MATH] parties, disproving a recent conjecture. We also show that, for mixtures of Dicke states, the PPT condition with respect to the most balanced bipartition implies all other PPT conditions. We further connect bosonic extendibility of mixtures of Dicke states to the duals of known hierarchies for non-negative polynomials, such as the ones by Reznick and Polya. We thus provide semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

.
tldr: Provides a complete mathematical theory for entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states, linking separability to completely positive tensors and disproving a conjecture about PPT entanglement.
motivation: To understand entanglement in the important subclass of Dicke states, which arise in bosonic systems, and to bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry.
method: Introduces a tensor-based parametrization where diagonal entries are encoded as symmetric tensors, mapping separability to completely positive tensors, PPT to moment tensors, and entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors.
result: Establishes existence of PPT entanglement for all multipartite systems with local dimension ≥3 and ≥3 parties, disproving a recent conjecture; shows PPT condition for most balanced bipartition implies all others; connects bosonic extendibility to hierarchies for non-negative polynomials.
conclusion: Provides semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace, advancing entanglement theory and its computational tools.

title: Measuring Rényi Entropy With An Echo Protocol
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2146 (2026).

We present efficient and practical protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy, whose exponential is known as the purity. Our approach is based on expressing the purity in terms of transition probabilities generated by an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, making it applicable to quantum many-body systems. Notably, our approach does not rely on random-noise averaging, a feature that can be extended to protocols to measure out-of-time-order correlation functions, as we demonstrate. By way of example, we show that our protocols can be practically implemented in superconducting qubit-based platforms, as well as in cavity-QED trapped ultra-cold gases.

.
tldr: Presents efficient echo-based protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy (purity) in quantum many-body systems without random-noise averaging.
motivation: Measuring Rényi entropy is crucial for characterizing entanglement and quantum correlations, but existing methods often require random averaging or are inefficient.
method: The purity is expressed in terms of transition probabilities from an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, avoiding random-noise averaging; the protocol is extended to out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The protocols are shown to be practically implementable on superconducting qubit platforms and in cavity-QED trapped ultracold gases.
conclusion: The work provides a practical, noise-robust method for measuring purity and OTOCs, advancing experimental quantum information processing.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: This paper tightly characterizes the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice states, providing nearly matching upper and lower bounds for all parameter regimes.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine in quantum computing, but its cost when given imperfect advice (states with partial overlap with the top eigenspace) was not well understood. The authors aim to close this gap.
method: The authors develop algorithms for phase estimation with advice and prove nearly matching lower bounds using the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials, as well as reductions from the unitary recurrence time problem.
result: They show that a small number of advice copies do not significantly help, and that having many copies does not reduce cost much either. They also derive a tight bound for error probability reduction in basic phase estimation.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the cost of phase estimation with advice, resolving open questions and offering insights into the power of quantum advice in this context.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity, showing that stabilizer states maximally violate it and linking Bell violation to Wigner negativity volume.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is important for understanding nonlocality, but known results for qubits do not directly extend to qudits.
method: The authors introduce a new CHSH-like inequality for qudits using correlations tied to Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under a generalized π/8 gate, and analyze its violation using stabilizer states and phase-diagonal unitaries.
result: A specific stabilizer state achieves maximal violation among all qudit states, and the Bell operator quantifies both singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume. Rational-phase diagonal unitaries reproduce CGLMP and SATWAP violations.
conclusion: Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems, and the proposed inequality provides a direct link between nonlocality and a quantum resource theory.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes that encode the combinatorial Laplacian, enabling superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: Classical algorithms for topological data analysis, such as computing persistent Betti numbers, are computationally expensive. Quantum walks offer a potential speedup, but previous approaches required oracles or lacked efficient constructions for simplicial complexes.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by operating on a doubled state space of oriented simplices, using coherent interference to project onto harmonic cycles. They provide efficient gate complexity for clique complexes and extend the framework to estimate persistent Betti numbers, verify QMA-hard problems, and solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem.
result: The quantum walk achieves an apparent superpolynomial speedup over classical algorithms, assuming an inverse-polynomially bounded spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling. The construction requires O(poly(n, 1/δ, log(1/ε))) gates.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a novel quantum advantage in topological data analysis without quantum oracles, opening new avenues for quantum algorithms in computational topology and complexity theory.

title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
authors: Vasco Cavina And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: This paper extends the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium Gaussian reservoirs, enabling the study of quantum thermodynamics with strong coupling and squeezed/displaced modes.
motivation: Standard quantum thermodynamics often assumes weak coupling or equilibrium reservoirs; this work aims to model realistic non-equilibrium environments and understand thermodynamic laws in such settings.
method: The authors introduce a non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model with squeezed and displaced thermal reservoirs, treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour, and compute heat statistics.
result: They show that strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can generate effective time dependence and pure work, and that the fluctuation-dissipation relation is broken but reconciled with the second law. A quantum-classical correspondence for heat statistics is established, and a fluctuation theorem for energy balance is proven.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile framework for quantum thermodynamics far from equilibrium, with implications for work extraction, heat statistics, and thermodynamic symmetries.

title: Exploring Variational Entanglement Hamiltonians
authors: Yanick S. Kind And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2133 (2026).

Recent advances in analog and digital quantum-simulation platforms have enabled exploration of the spectrum of entanglement Hamiltonians via variational algorithms. In this work we analyze the convergence properties of the variationally obtained solutions and compare them to numerically exact calculations in quantum critical systems. We demonstrate that interpreting the cost functional as an integral permits the deployment of iterative quadrature schemes, thereby reducing the required number of measurements by more than an order of magnitude even in the presence of noise. We further show that a modified ansatz captures deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models, improves convergence, improves trainability and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Finally, we establish that a low cost value does not by itself guarantee convergence in trace distance. Nevertheless, it faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps, which are essential for applications to topological phases.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes variational entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum critical systems, demonstrating improved convergence and measurement efficiency.
motivation: Understanding entanglement Hamiltonians is crucial for characterizing quantum phases, but their experimental extraction is challenging. Variational methods offer a practical approach, yet their convergence properties and reliability need systematic study.
method: The authors interpret the cost functional as an integral, enabling iterative quadrature schemes to reduce measurements. They also introduce a modified ansatz to capture deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models.
result: The proposed methods reduce required measurements by over an order of magnitude even with noise, improve convergence and trainability, and provide a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Low cost value does not guarantee convergence in trace distance but faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps.
conclusion: Variational entanglement Hamiltonians are a powerful tool for studying quantum phases, and the proposed techniques enhance their efficiency and reliability, particularly for topological phases.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to construct device-independent secure sequential quantum protocols from bipartite self-testing qubit protocols.
motivation: Sequential scenarios can enhance device-independent protocols by reusing quantum states, but a general construction method was lacking.
method: Replace one measurement in a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol with a non-projective measurement and add an additional user, then prove security analytically.
result: The resulting ideal correlations are secure against statistical mixture reproduction, enabling device-independent certification of randomness.
conclusion: The systematic recipe provides a foundation for developing new device-independent quantum security schemes.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: This paper shows that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite network state can estimate entanglement witnesses, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing measurement settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are crucial for verifying entanglement, but typically require changing measurement settings. The authors aim to simplify this by using a fixed measurement setting on a specially prepared network state.
method: The authors introduce a network state and a fixed measurement setting to estimate decomposable and non-decomposable entanglement witnesses, including those detecting bound entanglement. They extend the approach to multipartite graph states.
result: They demonstrate that decomposable EWs (equivalent to partial transpose criteria) can be estimated with a fixed setting, and also handle non-decomposable EWs for bound entanglement. The method applies to graph states and distributed settings.
conclusion: The work provides a practical, measurement-based method for entanglement verification that is resource-efficient and applicable to multipartite states and quantum networks.

title: Distributed Quantum Information Processing: A Review Of Recent Progress
authors: J Knörzer, X Liu, B F Schiffer And J Tura
abstract: Distributed quantum information processing seeks to overcome the scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication. This approach extends the capabilities of individual devices, enabling access to larger problem instances and novel algorithmic techniques. Beyond increasing qubit counts, it also enables qualitatively new capabilities, such as joint measurements on multiple copies of high-dimensional quantum states. The distinction between single-copy and multi-copy access reveals important differences in task complexity and helps identify which computational problems stand to benefit from distributed quantum resources. At the same time, it highlights trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and the practical challenges involved in realizing them experimentally. In this review, we contextualize recent developments by surveying the theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols and examining the experimental platforms and algorithmic applications that realize them in practice.
tldr: A comprehensive review of distributed quantum information processing, covering theoretical foundations, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
motivation: To overcome scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication.
method: Survey of theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
result: Identifies trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and practical challenges in realizing distributed quantum systems.
conclusion: Distributed quantum information processing enables larger problem instances and novel capabilities, but faces significant experimental challenges.

title: Precise Computation Of Universal Corner Entanglement Entropy At 2+1 Dimension: From Ising To Gaussian Quantum Critical Points
authors: Ben Lee-Yeung Ngai, Justin Tim-Lok Chau, Junchen Rong, Meng Cheng, Yuan Da Liao And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes the universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel QMC algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
motivation: Computing subleading logarithmic terms in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum states and critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to compute the 2nd Rényi entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The QMC results match the theoretical corner logarithmic term for the Gaussian tricritical point, and provide consistent results for the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: The algorithm successfully bridges the gap between exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes, establishing a long-sought connection for universal corner entanglement entropy in (2+1)d.

authors: Yizhi Luo

tldr: Achieving millisecond coherence times in gigahertz-frequency mechanical oscillators by removing subsurface damage.

result: Coherence times exceeding 1 millisecond are demonstrated at gigahertz frequencies, a significant improvement over previous devices.
conclusion: Subsurface damage is a major decoherence source; its removal enables high-coherence mechanical oscillators for quantum applications.

title: Hybrid Nanophotonic Trap For Cold Atoms Using Surface Forces And A Blue-detuned Evanescent Field
authors: Riccardo Pennetta

motivation: To improve the performance of atom-based quantum devices by combining nanophotonics with cold atoms, addressing challenges in loading efficiency and coherence.
method: The trap uses surface forces (Casimir-Polder) for attraction and a blue-detuned evanescent field for repulsion, creating a stable potential for cold caesium atoms near a nanophotonic waveguide.
result: Demonstrated efficient loading, long storage times, and enhanced coherence times compared to previous traps.
conclusion: This hybrid approach offers a promising platform for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems, integrating cold atoms with nanophotonic circuits.

title: Doubly-polylog-time-overhead Fault-tolerant Quantum Computation By A Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect Matching Decoder
authors: Yugo Takada
Hayata Yamasaki
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme with doubly polylogarithmic time overhead using a polylog-time parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient decoding algorithms to correct errors with minimal time overhead, which is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The authors develop a parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder that runs in polylogarithmic time and integrate it into a fault-tolerant protocol to achieve doubly polylogarithmic time overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with time overhead scaling as O(polylog(n)) for both the decoder and the overall protocol, significantly improving over previous polynomial overheads.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that polylog-time decoding is possible for fault-tolerant quantum computation, bringing practical quantum computing closer to reality.

A fundamental challenge in multiparameter quantum estimation arises from the incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, leading to intricate precision trade-offs that obscure the understanding of ultimate quantum limits. Here, we present an approach that precisely quantifies t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to precisely quantify the minimal trade-off and identify optimal measurements for multiparameter quantum estimation.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces precision trade-offs due to incompatible optimal measurements, obscuring ultimate quantum limits.
method: The authors develop an approach that quantifies the trade-off and finds optimal measurements using information-theoretic tools.
result: They derive tight bounds on achievable precision and demonstrate the optimal measurement strategy for several examples.
conclusion: The work provides a clear framework for understanding and optimizing multiparameter estimation, advancing quantum metrology.

authors: Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:

Studies of entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems have focused largely on initial product states. Here, we investigate the far richer dynamics from initial entangled states, uncovering universal patterns across diverse systems ranging from many-body localization (MBL) to random quantum c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics from initial entangled states in many-body systems, revealing universal patterns across MBL and random quantum circuits.
motivation: Previous studies focused on product states; understanding dynamics from entangled initial states is crucial for quantum information processing and thermalization.
method: The authors numerically simulate entanglement growth in various models, including MBL and random circuits, starting from entangled states, and analyze the scaling behavior.
result: They find universal features in entanglement growth that depend on the initial entanglement structure, with distinct regimes for MBL and ergodic systems.
conclusion: Initial entanglement significantly alters entanglement dynamics, providing a unified perspective on entanglement generation and transport.

title: Unbounded Sequence Of Observers Exhibiting Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Steering Via Probabilistic Projective Measurements
authors: Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, And Hui-Juan Zuo
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Hong Song, Bang-Hai Wang, Zhi-Hua Chen, Zhihao Ma, and Hui-Juan Zuo

Recent studies have demonstrated that coherent weak measurements allow Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering to be shared sequentially between a single Alice and multiple Bobs. Theoretically, this permits an unbounded sequence in the high-dimensional limit. In this work, we investigate whether the experi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012411] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering can be shared among an unbounded sequence of observers using probabilistic projective measurements, extending previous results with weak measurements.
motivation: To determine whether the sequential sharing of EPR steering, previously demonstrated with weak measurements, can also be achieved with projective measurements, which are more experimentally accessible.
method: The authors propose a protocol using probabilistic projective measurements on a single Alice and multiple Bobs, and analyze the steering sharing condition using a linear steering inequality.
result: They prove that an unbounded sequence of Bobs can demonstrate steering with Alice, provided the measurement outcomes are postselected, and the number of Bobs increases with the dimension of the shared entangled state.
conclusion: Probabilistic projective measurements can enable unbounded sequential sharing of EPR steering, offering a practical alternative to weak measurements for demonstrating this phenomenon.

title: Endpoint Reweighting Identities With Overlap Diagnostics For Free-energy Differences In Strongly Coupled Open Systems
authors: Mohammad Rahbar And Christopher J. Stein
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Rahbar and Christopher J. Stein

We develop a reweighting framework to quantify the free energy difference between two equilibrium states of a strongly coupled open system at fixed temperature. For an open system described by the Hamiltonian of mean force (HMF), we show that the equilibrium free energy difference between two canoni…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014113] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a reweighting framework using the Hamiltonian of mean force to compute free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems.
motivation: Computing free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems is challenging due to the breakdown of standard methods; a rigorous framework is needed.
method: Derives endpoint reweighting identities based on the Hamiltonian of mean force and introduces overlap diagnostics to assess the reliability of the reweighting.
result: The identities allow accurate estimation of free energy differences even under strong coupling, with overlap diagnostics providing a measure of confidence.
conclusion: The framework extends free energy calculation methods to strongly coupled regimes, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the precision of parameter estimation near quantum phase transitions, considering the trade-off between critical enhancement and slowing down.
result: Identifies a universal scaling limit that constrains the precision achievable in finite-time critical metrology.
conclusion: The bound provides a fundamental limitation for critical quantum metrology, guiding optimal design of metrological protocols.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a statistical learning method to verify approximate k-designs using randomized measurements, reducing measurement resources.
motivation: Verifying that a quantum state ensemble forms an approximate k-design is crucial for many quantum information tasks, but existing methods require many measurements. A more efficient verification protocol is needed.
method: The authors use randomized measurements and a classical machine learning model trained on measurement outcomes to classify whether the ensemble is an approximate k-design, leveraging statistical learning theory.
result: The method achieves high accuracy with significantly fewer measurements than traditional approaches, and is robust to noise and imperfections.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and resource-efficient tool for certifying random state ensembles, with applications in quantum benchmarking and many-body physics.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms

abstract:

result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is utilizable for simulating complex quantum dynamics, with high-fidelity state preparation and readout.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom platform is a viable candidate for demonstrating practical quantum advantage in simulating many-body physics.

authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B.
