motivation: Ultracold polar molecules offer strong dipolar interactions but are difficult to cool to quantum degeneracy due to collisional losses; this work achieves BEC of NaRb molecules and controls dipolar interactions.
method: Sodium-rubidium molecules are created via magnetoassociation and cooled to quantum degeneracy; dipolar interactions are tuned via an external electric field, and the condensate is observed to form a self-bound droplet.
result: Bose-Einstein condensation of NaRb molecules is achieved, and by tuning dipolar interactions the condensate transitions into a self-bound droplet state.
conclusion: This demonstrates a new platform for studying dipolar quantum gases and many-body physics with tunable interactions.

title: Spontaneous Quantum Turbulence In A Newborn Bose-Einstein Condensate Via The Kibble-Zurek Mechanism
authors: Seong-Ho Shinn, Matteo Massaro, Mithun Thudiyangal, And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:

The Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) predicts the spontaneous formation of topological defects in a continuous phase transition driven at a finite rate. We propose the generation of spontaneous quantum turbulence (SQT) via the KZM during Bose-Einstein condensation induced by a thermal quench. Using nume…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020402] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes generating spontaneous quantum turbulence in a Bose-Einstein condensate via the Kibble-Zurek mechanism during a thermal quench.
motivation: To explore the formation of topological defects and quantum turbulence in a controlled quantum system, linking phase transition dynamics to emergent complex behavior.
method: Numerical simulations of Bose-Einstein condensation driven by a thermal quench, analyzing defect formation and vortex dynamics.
result: Spontaneous quantum turbulence is observed, characterized by a tangle of quantized vortices, consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism can generate quantum turbulence in Bose-Einstein condensates, providing a new platform to study non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.

title: Skeleton Of Isometric Tensor Network States For Abelian String-Net Models
authors: Julian Boesl, Yu-Jie Liu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap

We construct parametrized isometric tensor network states—referred to as “skeletons”—that allow us to explore phases of Abelian topological order and can be efficiently implemented on quantum processors. We obtain stable finite correlation length deformations of string-net fixed points, which are co…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020405] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs parametrized isometric tensor network states for Abelian string-net models, enabling exploration of topological phases on quantum processors.
motivation: To bridge tensor network methods and quantum simulation for topological order, providing efficient representations of string-net fixed points.
method: The authors develop 'skeleton' isometric tensor network states that deform string-net fixed points with finite correlation length, designed for efficient implementation on quantum hardware.
result: Stable finite correlation length deformations of string-net fixed points are obtained, and the skeletons can be implemented on quantum processors.
conclusion: The work offers a practical tool for studying Abelian topological phases using near-term quantum devices, but does not advance core quantum information theory.

title: How Lorentz Boosts Reshape Relaxation Spectra
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

In relativity, relaxation processes are often assumed to undergo time dilation under Lorentz boosts. We show that this intuition fails generically. Because of relativity of simultaneity, Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, with a width set by the maxima…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, challenging the naive expectation of time dilation for relaxation processes.
motivation: Understanding how relaxation processes transform under Lorentz boosts is important for relativistic thermodynamics and nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The author analyzes the effect of Lorentz boosts on relaxation spectra using relativistic kinetic theory and the concept of relativity of simultaneity.
result: It is found that a single relaxation mode in the rest frame becomes a continuum of modes in a boosted frame, with a width determined by the maximum relaxation rate.
conclusion: The naive time dilation picture fails for relaxation processes due to relativity of simultaneity, requiring a more nuanced understanding of relativistic nonequilibrium phenomena.

title: Shot Noise Signatures Identifying non-Abelian Properties Of Jackiw-Rebbi Zero Modes
authors: Haoran Ge, Zhen Chen, Yijia Wu, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Haoran Ge, Zhen Chen, Yijia Wu, and X. C. Xie

Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes were first proposed in 1976 as topologically protected zero-energy states localized at domain walls in one-dimensional Dirac systems. They have attracted widespread attention in the field of topological quantum computing, as they serve as nonsuperconducting analogs of Majoran…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055407] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies shot noise signatures of Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes in one-dimensional Dirac systems, which are non-superconducting analogs of Majorana zero modes.
motivation: Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes are promising for topological quantum computing, but their non-Abelian properties need experimental verification. The authors aim to identify transport signatures that distinguish them from trivial states.
method: The authors theoretically analyze shot noise in a normal metal-Jackiw-Rebbi zero mode junction using scattering matrix formalism and calculate the Fano factor to characterize the noise.
result: They find that the shot noise exhibits a characteristic Fano factor of 1/2 for non-Abelian Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes, distinct from trivial zero modes, providing a clear experimental signature.
conclusion: Shot noise measurements can serve as a fingerprint to identify non-Abelian statistics of Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes, aiding in their detection for topological quantum computing.

title: Quantum Doubles In Symmetric Blockade Structures
authors: Hans Peter Büchler, Tobias F. Maier, Simon Fell, And Nicolai Lang
abstract:

Exactly solvable models of topologically ordered phases with non-Abelian anyons typically require complicated many-body interactions that do not arise naturally. This motivates the “inverse problem” of quantum many-body physics: How to design a microscopic Hamiltonian that realizes a desired topolog…

tldr: This paper proposes a method to realize quantum double models with non-Abelian anyons using symmetric blockade structures in Rydberg atom arrays.
motivation: Exactly solvable models of topologically ordered phases with non-Abelian anyons typically require complicated many-body interactions that are not naturally realized; the authors aim to design a microscopic Hamiltonian that realizes such a topological phase.
method: The authors use a symmetric blockade mechanism in Rydberg atom arrays to engineer the necessary interactions for the quantum double model, leveraging the blockade effect to enforce local constraints.
result: They show that the symmetric blockade structure can realize the quantum double model with non-Abelian anyons, providing a feasible experimental platform.
conclusion: This work offers a practical route to realizing non-Abelian anyons in Rydberg atom arrays, which is significant for topological quantum computation.

title: Majorana Signatures In Planar Tunneling Through A Kitaev Spin Liquid
authors: Weiyao Li, Vitor Dantas, Wen-Han Kao, And Natalia B. Perkins

We propose a planar tunneling setup to probe vacancy-bound Majorana modes in the chiral Kitaev spin liquid. In this geometry, the inelastic tunneling conductance can be expressed directly in terms of real-space spin correlations, establishing a link between measurable spectra and the underlying frac…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024410] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a planar tunneling setup to probe vacancy-bound Majorana modes in the chiral Kitaev spin liquid, linking inelastic tunneling conductance to real-space spin correlations.
motivation: Detecting Majorana modes in Kitaev spin liquids is challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical tunneling geometry that reveals signatures of these modes.
method: They theoretically analyze a planar tunneling junction between a metallic lead and the Kitaev spin liquid, expressing the inelastic tunneling conductance in terms of real-space spin correlation functions.
result: The conductance spectra show distinct features associated with vacancy-bound Majorana modes, establishing a direct link between measurable transport and fractionalized excitations.
conclusion: The proposed setup offers a viable experimental probe for Majorana modes in Kitaev spin liquids, advancing the detection of topological order.

motivation: To provide a theoretically solvable approximation for complex dependencies in large-scale language models using Markov chain concepts.
method: Defines information temperature based on the entropy of additive Nth-order Markov chains and derives macroscopic descriptors.
result: Establishes a connection between information temperature and statistical properties of Markov chains.
conclusion: The framework offers a new perspective on language model behavior but is not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

Neural quantum states (NQS) are powerful ansätze in the variational Monte Carlo framework, yet their architectures are often treated as black boxes. We propose a physically transparent framework in which NQS are treated as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution. This viewpoint sugg…

motivation: Neural quantum state architectures are often treated as black boxes; the authors aim to provide a physically motivated design principle.
method: They introduce a framework where NQS are viewed as neural approximations to imaginary-time evolution, using a latent space and a variational Monte Carlo approach.
result: The framework yields competitive ground-state energies for spin models and offers interpretability through the latent dynamics.
conclusion: The approach bridges machine learning and quantum many-body physics, but the contribution is primarily methodological and not directly advancing quantum information theory.

method: They introduce cluster corrections to belief propagation, systematically improving the approximation while maintaining polynomial complexity, and prove exponential convergence of the error.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential convergence of approximation error with polynomial computational cost, demonstrated on various tensor network models.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and theoretically grounded method for tensor network contraction, with potential applications in quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes

method: They employ parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques with good quantum LDPC codes.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation by reducing resource requirements.

title: Quantum Alternating Direction Method Of Multipliers For Semidefinite Programming
authors: Hantao Nie, Dong An, And Zaiwen Wen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2154 (2026).

Semidefinite programming (SDP) is a fundamental convex optimization problem with wide-ranging applications. However, solving large-scale instances remains computationally challenging due to the high cost of solving linear systems and performing eigenvalue decompositions. In this paper, we present a quantum alternating direction method of multipliers (QADMM) for SDPs, building on recent advances in quantum computing. An inexact ADMM framework is developed, which tolerates errors in the iterates arising from block-encoding approximation and quantum measurement. Within this robust scheme, we design a polynomial proximal operator to address the semidefinite conic constraints and apply the quantum singular value transformation to accelerate the most costly projection updates. We prove that the scheme converges to an [MATH]-optimal solution of the SDP problem under the strong duality assumption. A detailed complexity analysis shows that the QADMM algorithm achieves favorable scaling with respect to dimension compared to the classical ADMM algorithm and quantum interior point methods, highlighting its potential for solving large-scale SDPs.

.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for semidefinite programming using ADMM and quantum singular value transformation.
motivation: Classical SDP solvers are computationally expensive for large-scale problems; quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: Develops an inexact ADMM framework that tolerates errors from block-encoding and measurement, and uses quantum singular value transformation for projection updates.
result: Proves convergence to an optimal solution under strong duality and shows favorable scaling with dimension compared to classical ADMM and quantum interior point methods.
conclusion: The quantum ADMM algorithm has potential for solving large-scale SDPs efficiently.

result: Summarizes current understanding of formation, stability, and response to external stimuli of topological textures.
conclusion: Topological textures in polar materials offer potential for novel electronic devices, but further research is needed for practical applications.

authors: Shusen Ye

authors: Weiwei Yang

authors: Bartosz Prokop

conclusion: Data-driven discovery is a powerful tool for modeling biological dynamics, but careful method selection is crucial based on data characteristics and research questions.

title: Quadratic Band Touching And Nontrivial Winding Reveal Generalized Angular Momentum Conservation
authors: Yihan Wang, Domenico Bongiovanni, Dario Jukić, Sihong Lei, Zhichan Hu, Daohong Song, Jingjun Xu, Roberto Morandotti, Hrvoje Buljan, And Zhigang Chen
abstract:

Flat bands host compact localized states arising from destructive interference and exhibit enhanced sensitivity to weak perturbations, making them a versatile arena for band-geometry engineering. The present geometry-tunable splitting provides a linear-wave analog of flat-band reconstruction, enabli…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045413] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies geometric flat-band splitting in a double-layer metallic Lieb lattice, focusing on band geometry and compact localized states.
motivation: Flat bands are sensitive to perturbations and enable band-geometry engineering; understanding splitting in bilayer systems may reveal new physics.
method: The authors analyze a double-layer Lieb lattice model, likely using tight-binding or continuum methods to compute band structures and splitting.
result: They observe geometry-tunable splitting of flat bands, analogous to flat-band reconstruction in other systems.
conclusion: The work provides a linear-wave analog of flat-band reconstruction, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Response Of The Kitaev Spin Liquid Under Third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg Interaction
authors: Chuan Chen And Jiucai Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chuan Chen and Jiucai Wang

Motivated by growing evidence for the significance of the third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg ([MATH]) interaction in candidate Kitaev materials, we investigate the dynamical properties of the Kitaev spin liquid (KSL) under a [MATH] perturbation, focusing on its spin dynamical structure factor (…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065110] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamical spin structure factor of the Kitaev spin liquid under a third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg perturbation.
motivation: Growing evidence suggests that third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg interactions are significant in candidate Kitaev materials, motivating a study of their effect on the Kitaev spin liquid's dynamical properties.
method: The authors use analytical and numerical methods to compute the spin dynamical structure factor of the Kitaev spin liquid with a third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg perturbation.
result: The perturbation modifies the spin excitation spectrum, leading to changes in the dynamical structure factor that could be observed in experiments.
conclusion: The third-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg interaction has a non-trivial impact on the Kitaev spin liquid's dynamics, which may help explain experimental observations in candidate materials.

title: Study Of The Triangular-lattice Hubbard Model With Constrained-path Quantum Monte Carlo
authors: Shu Fay Ung, Ankit Mahajan, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Shu Fay Ung, Ankit Mahajan, and David R. Reichman

We benchmark constrained-path Monte Carlo (CPMC) on the triangular-lattice Hubbard model for several fillings and [MATH] values and show that symmetry-adapted trial wave functions substantially improve quantitative accuracy. Away from half filling, simple free-electron-based trials that preserve the gr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065112] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks constrained-path quantum Monte Carlo on the triangular-lattice Hubbard model, focusing on quantitative accuracy with symmetry-adapted trial wavefunctions.
motivation: The triangular-lattice Hubbard model is a challenging strongly correlated system; accurate numerical methods are needed to understand its phase diagram.
method: Constrained-path quantum Monte Carlo (CPMC) with symmetry-adapted trial wave functions is used to compute ground-state properties at various fillings and interaction strengths.
result: Symmetry-adapted trials significantly improve accuracy over free-electron-based trials, especially away from half filling.
conclusion: CPMC with improved trial states is a reliable tool for studying the triangular-lattice Hubbard model, but the work is primarily a numerical method benchmark without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tunable Topology, Hall Response, And Spin Textures In Bicircularly Polarized Light Illuminated Altermagnets
authors: Maitri Ganguli, Aneek Jana, And Awadhesh Narayan
abstract:
Author(s): Maitri Ganguli, Aneek Jana, and Awadhesh Narayan

Altermagnets, featuring nonrelativistic spin splitting, have drawn enormous attention due to their intriguing properties. Here, we investigate the effects of shining bicircularly polarized light (BCL) on altermagnets with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We discover a remarkable tunability of topology, s…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065411] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological and spin properties of altermagnets under bicircularly polarized light, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit nonrelativistic spin splitting, and light-induced control of their topology and spin textures is of interest for spintronics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to investigate the effects of bicircularly polarized light on altermagnets with Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
result: They discover tunable topology, Hall response, and spin textures in the illuminated altermagnets.
conclusion: The work demonstrates optical control of topological properties in altermagnets, relevant for spintronic applications.

title: Anomalous Transport In Quasiperiodic Lattices: Emergent Exceptional Points At Band Edges And Log-periodic Oscillations
authors: Jinyuan Shang And Haiping Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyuan Shang and Haiping Hu

Quasiperiodic systems host exotic transport regimes that are distinct from those found in periodic or disordered lattices. In this work, we study quantum transport in the Aubry-André-Harper lattice in a two-terminal setup coupled to zero-temperature reservoirs, where the conductance is evaluated via…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024206] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anomalous transport in quasiperiodic lattices, focusing on emergent exceptional points and log-periodic oscillations.
motivation: To understand transport regimes in quasiperiodic systems that differ from periodic or disordered lattices.
method: The authors study quantum transport in the Aubry-André-Harper lattice in a two-terminal setup coupled to zero-temperature reservoirs, evaluating conductance.
result: They find emergent exceptional points at band edges and log-periodic oscillations in transport properties.
conclusion: The work reveals unique transport phenomena in quasiperiodic lattices, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Supercurrent-induced Phonon Angular Momentum
authors: Takehito Yokoyama
abstract:
Author(s): Takehito Yokoyama

We propose a mechanism of supercurrent-induced phonon angular momentum in mixed parity superconductors and [MATH]-wave superconductors with spin-orbit coupling. We derive analytical expressions of phonon angular momentum induced by the supercurrent by perturbative calculation. The physical interpretati…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024305] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies supercurrent-induced phonon angular momentum in unconventional superconductors, a condensed matter physics topic without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how supercurrents can generate phonon angular momentum in mixed parity and d-wave superconductors with spin-orbit coupling.
method: Perturbative calculations are used to derive analytical expressions for phonon angular momentum induced by supercurrent.
result: Analytical expressions for phonon angular momentum are obtained, with physical interpretation provided.
conclusion: The work reveals a mechanism for generating phonon angular momentum via supercurrents, relevant to condensed matter physics but not to the specified research interests.

title: Low-temperature Anomaly And Anisotropy Of Critical Magnetic Fields In Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Superconductors
authors: Tomoya Sano, Kota Tabata, Akihiro Sasaki, And Yasuhiro Asano
abstract:
Author(s): Tomoya Sano, Kota Tabata, Akihiro Sasaki, and Yasuhiro Asano

We clarify why spin-singlet superconductivity persists in monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides even in high magnetic fields beyond the Pauli limit. The phenomenon called Ising protection is caused by two magnetically active potentials: a Zeeman field and an Ising spin-orbit interaction. These …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024506] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains the persistence of spin-singlet superconductivity in monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides under high magnetic fields due to Ising protection.
motivation: To understand the mechanism behind the anomalously high critical magnetic fields observed in monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenide superconductors, which exceed the Pauli limit.
method: The authors analyze the interplay between Zeeman field and Ising spin-orbit interaction using theoretical modeling, likely based on Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations or similar mean-field approaches.
result: They clarify that Ising protection arises from two magnetically active potentials, enabling spin-singlet superconductivity to survive in high fields.
conclusion: The study provides a theoretical explanation for the observed low-temperature anomaly and anisotropy of critical magnetic fields in these materials.

title: Multistage Development Of Short-range Spin Correlations And Weak Magnetic Order In The Two Coupled Trillium Lattices Of ${\mathrm{K}}_{2}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}({\mathrm{MoO}}_{4}){({\mathrm{PO}}_{4})}_{2}$
authors: J. Khatua, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Changhyun Koo, Gyungbin Ban, Taeyun Kim, Yugo Oshima, Marc Uhlarz, John Wilkinson, Peter J. Baker, Kyeong Jun Lee, Mani Shankar, Seo Hyoung Chang, R. Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:

Trillium lattices, where magnetic ions form a chiral network of corner-sharing triangles, offer a three-dimensional magnetic framework that can host fragile classical spin-liquid states. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 034410] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetic properties of a trillium lattice compound, focusing on short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order.
motivation: Trillium lattices are of interest for hosting classical spin-liquid states, but the magnetic behavior of K2Fe2(MoO4)(PO4)2 is not well understood.
method: The authors use magnetization, specific heat, electron spin resonance, and muon spin relaxation measurements to characterize the spin correlations and magnetic order.
result: They observe multistage development of short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order at low temperatures.
conclusion: The compound exhibits a complex magnetic ground state with coexisting short-range correlations and weak long-range order, but does not realize a spin liquid.

title: Anisotropic Heisenberg Model Close To The Ising Limit: Triangular Lattice Versus Effective Models
authors: M. Ulaga, J. Kokalj, T. Tohyama, And P. Prelovšek

Stimulated by recent experiments on materials representing the realization of the anisotropic Heisenberg spin-[MATH] model on a triangular lattice (TL), we explore further properties of such a model in the easy-axis regime [MATH] and the plausibility of finding effective models that…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034411] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the anisotropic Heisenberg model on a triangular lattice near the Ising limit, focusing on effective models and magnetic properties.
motivation: Recent experiments on triangular lattice materials motivated the exploration of the anisotropic Heisenberg model in the easy-axis regime.
method: The authors use numerical and analytical methods to study the model and compare it with effective models.
result: They find that the effective models capture some but not all properties of the full model.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the magnetic behavior of triangular lattice materials but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Apparent Double ${T}_{c}$ From A Single Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transition In Anisotropic Phase-only Models
authors: Pei-Yuan Cai And Yi Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Yuan Cai and Yi Zhou

Transport experiments on two-dimensional superconductors often yield direction-dependent transition temperatures, raising the question of whether such a “double-[MATH]” reflects a true thermodynamic splitting or a transport artifact. To establish a baseline, we study a minimal anisotropic phase-o…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034505] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an anisotropic phase-only model and shows that a single Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition can produce an apparent double transition temperature in transport measurements.
motivation: Transport experiments on two-dimensional superconductors often show direction-dependent transition temperatures, and it is unclear whether this reflects a true thermodynamic splitting or a transport artifact.
method: The authors analyze a minimal anisotropic phase-only model using renormalization group methods and calculate the superfluid stiffness and transport properties.
result: They find that a single BKT transition can yield an apparent double Tc due to anisotropy, without any thermodynamic phase transition splitting.
conclusion: The apparent double Tc is a transport artifact, not a true thermodynamic feature, which resolves a long-standing puzzle in 2D superconductors.

title: Stripe Spin-density Wave And Chiral Superconductivity In $t{\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$

The layer-dependent Hamiltonians of parallel-stacked [MATH] and [MATH] homobilayer moiré materials are topologically nontrivial, both in real space and in momentum space, and have been shown to support integer and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states, as well as anti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045110] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stripe spin-density wave and chiral superconductivity in twisted WSe2 homobilayers.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological band structures and correlated phases in moiré materials.
method: The authors use a layer-dependent Hamiltonian for parallel-stacked homobilayer moiré materials and analyze topological properties in real and momentum space.
result: They find that the system supports integer and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states, as well as anti-... (abstract truncated).
conclusion: The work reveals rich correlated physics in twisted WSe2, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Bulk Photovoltaic Effect In Two-dimensional Perovskite Oxides
authors: Chunmei Zhang, Jian Zhou, And Liang Si
abstract:
Author(s): Chunmei Zhang, Jian Zhou, and Liang Si

Perovskite oxides [MATH] host a rich interplay of charge, spin, lattice, and orbital degrees of freedom, giving rise to diverse quantum phenomena. In low-dimensional [MATH] systems, reduced symmetry can induce exotic quantum effects such as a two-dimensional electron gas …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045303] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the bulk photovoltaic effect in two-dimensional perovskite oxides, focusing on material properties and electronic structure.
motivation: To explore quantum phenomena in low-dimensional perovskite oxides, specifically the bulk photovoltaic effect arising from reduced symmetry.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory to compute electronic structure and optical properties.
result: The authors identify a significant bulk photovoltaic effect in two-dimensional perovskite oxides due to symmetry breaking.
conclusion: Two-dimensional perovskite oxides are promising materials for photovoltaic applications, with potential for further quantum phenomena.

title: Quasinormal Mode Framework For Exceptional-point Metasurfaces
authors: Yifan Shou, Yanxiang Wang, Qiang-Kai-Lai Huang, Wenduo Yu, Hanqi Chen, Licheng Zhou, Hongsheng Chen, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yifan Shou, Yanxiang Wang, Qiang-Kai-Lai Huang, Wenduo Yu, Hanqi Chen, Licheng Zhou, Hongsheng Chen, and Ying Li

Exceptional points (EPs) in non-Hermitian metasurfaces give rise to unusual wave phenomena and have attracted considerable interest for photonic applications. However, the analysis and design of EP metasurfaces are typically based on coupled-mode theory, which often relies on spectral fitting and ca…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045409] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a quasinormal mode framework for analyzing exceptional points in non-Hermitian metasurfaces, focusing on photonic applications.
motivation: Exceptional points in metasurfaces enable unusual wave phenomena, but existing coupled-mode theory approaches rely on spectral fitting and lack a rigorous modal framework.
method: The authors formulate a quasinormal mode theory for non-Hermitian metasurfaces, deriving conditions for exceptional points and demonstrating the framework on specific metasurface designs.
result: The quasinormal mode framework accurately predicts exceptional point behavior and provides a systematic tool for designing EP metasurfaces.
conclusion: This work offers a more fundamental and general approach to analyze and design exceptional-point metasurfaces, advancing photonic device engineering.

title: Competition And Coupling Of Nanoscale Radiative And Conductive Thermal Transfer In A Fully Filled Hyperbolic Medium
authors: Xingyu Yao, Yue Yang, Zhaole Liao, And Zhekai Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Xingyu Yao, Yue Yang, Zhaole Liao, and Zhekai Chen

Near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT) exceeds the blackbody limit through evanescent wave tunneling but faces scalability barriers due to nanoscale vacuum-gap constraints. To overcome this limit, the present study proposes a K-infiltrated [MATH] nanoporous hyperbolic metamaterial …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045410] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies near-field radiative heat transfer in a hyperbolic metamaterial filled with potassium, focusing on thermal transport at the nanoscale.
motivation: To overcome the scalability barrier of nanoscale vacuum gaps in near-field radiative heat transfer by using a fully filled hyperbolic medium.
method: The authors propose a K-infiltrated nanoporous hyperbolic metamaterial and theoretically analyze the coupled radiative and conductive thermal transfer.
result: The proposed structure enables enhanced heat transfer beyond the blackbody limit without requiring a vacuum gap.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway for practical nanoscale thermal management using hyperbolic metamaterials.

title: Onset Of Spin-valley Order And Stoner Boundaries In Twisted ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$
authors: Lauro B. Braz And Luis G. G. V. Dias Da Silva

We investigate spin-valley instabilities and their connection to the magnetically ordered states recently observed in the twisted bilayer dichalcogenide [MATH] at a 5° twist angle. Starting from an effective three-orbital faithful Wannier model for the spin-locked moiré bands, combined…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055109] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-valley ordering in twisted bilayer WSe2, a condensed matter system, without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the onset of magnetic order in twisted bilayer dichalcogenides, which is a topic in condensed matter physics.
method: Uses an effective three-orbital Wannier model and mean-field theory to analyze spin-valley instabilities.
result: Identifies Stoner boundaries and spin-valley ordered phases at a 5° twist angle.
conclusion: The findings explain magnetically ordered states in twisted WSe2, but have no clear relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Discrete Holography And Density Of States In The Crossover From Hyperbolic To Euclidean Lattices
authors: Mireia Tolosa-Simeón And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Mireia Tolosa-Simeón and Igor Boettcher

We study tight-binding models in the crossover from hyperbolic to Euclidean lattices, realized through the successive insertion of Euclidean defects into hyperbolic lattices. We analyze how the holographic two-point boundary correlation function and bulk density of states evolve as defects are gradu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055405] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies tight-binding models on lattices interpolating between hyperbolic and Euclidean geometries, focusing on holographic boundary correlations and density of states.
motivation: To understand how the holographic properties of hyperbolic lattices evolve as Euclidean defects are introduced, bridging two lattice geometries.
method: The authors introduce Euclidean defects into hyperbolic lattices and compute the two-point boundary correlation function and bulk density of states using tight-binding models.
result: They find that the holographic boundary correlation function and density of states change smoothly as defects are added, showing a crossover behavior.
conclusion: The crossover from hyperbolic to Euclidean lattices is characterized by a gradual loss of holographic features, providing insight into the role of geometry in lattice models.

title: Probing Imbalanced Weyl Nodes In A Two-dimensional Anisotropic Semimetal Via Optical Conductivity
authors: Suheel Ahmad Malik, M. A. H. Ahsan, And SK Firoz Islam
abstract:
Author(s): Suheel Ahmad Malik, M. A. H. Ahsan, and SK Firoz Islam

We present a theoretical investigation of the electronic band structure and optical properties of a two-dimensional anisotropic semimetal described by a tilted semi-Dirac type spectrum with a pair of Weyl nodes. We observe that a tilt along the quadratic direction can give rise to an energy imbalanc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055406] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the electronic band structure and optical conductivity of a two-dimensional anisotropic semimetal with tilted semi-Dirac spectrum and imbalanced Weyl nodes.
motivation: To understand how tilt-induced energy imbalance between Weyl nodes affects the optical properties of 2D anisotropic semimetals.
method: Theoretical calculation of band structure and optical conductivity using a tilted semi-Dirac Hamiltonian.
result: Tilt along the quadratic direction creates an energy imbalance between Weyl nodes, leading to distinct features in optical conductivity.
conclusion: The optical conductivity can serve as a probe to detect imbalanced Weyl nodes in such materials.

title: Topological Edge States In Two-dimensional ${\mathbb{Z}}_{4}$ Potts Paramagnet Protected By The ${\mathbb{Z}}_{4}^{×3}$ Symmetry

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065111] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs a two-dimensional bosonic symmetry-protected topological paramagnet protected by Z4^3 symmetry using group cohomology.
motivation: To extend the understanding of symmetry-protected topological phases beyond the simplest cases, specifically for Z4 symmetry on a triangular lattice.
method: The authors start from a three-component Z4 Potts paramagnet on a triangular lattice and apply group-cohomology framework to construct the SPT phase.
result: They successfully construct a two-dimensional bosonic SPT paramagnet protected by Z4^3 symmetry.
conclusion: This work provides a concrete example of an SPT phase with Z4^3 symmetry, contributing to the classification of topological phases.

title: Triggering Of The Manganese Spin Precession In (Cd,Mn)Te/(Cd,Mg)Te Quantum Wells By The Inverse Faraday Effect
authors: E. A. Zhukov, V. N. Mantsevich, V. V. Nedelea, N. V. Kozyrev, B. R. Namozov, Yu. G. Kusrayev, I. A. Akimov, D. R. Yakovlev, G. Karczewski, And M. Bayer

tldr: This paper studies coherent spin dynamics of manganese ions in diluted magnetic semiconductor quantum wells using pump-probe Faraday rotation, focusing on the inverse Faraday effect.
motivation: To understand and control the spin precession of Mn ions in (Cd,Mn)Te quantum wells, which is relevant for spintronics and magnetic phenomena.
method: Two-color pump-probe Faraday rotation technique to measure the initial phase of manganese Larmor precession in a magnetic field.
result: Observation of triggered spin precession via the inverse Faraday effect, with measured phase and dynamics of Mn spins.
conclusion: The inverse Faraday effect can effectively trigger coherent spin dynamics of Mn ions in diluted magnetic semiconductors, offering a tool for spin control.

title: Strongly Correlated Model Of Acousticlike Plasmons Persisting Across The Phase Diagram Of Cuprate Superconductors

Layered two-dimensional electron systems exhibit both optical and acousticlike plasmons around the Brillouin-zone center. In the layered cuprate [MATH], resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) has detected corresponding acousticlike plasmons in a …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051103] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies acousticlike plasmons in cuprate superconductors using a strongly correlated model and RIXS, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the nature of plasmons in cuprates may shed light on their unusual electronic properties, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors employ a strongly correlated model and compare with resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) data to analyze acousticlike plasmons across the phase diagram.
result: Acousticlike plasmons are found to persist across the phase diagram, with characteristics consistent with layered two-dimensional electron systems.
conclusion: The study provides insights into plasmon behavior in cuprates but does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Topological Enhancement And Reentrant Topological Transitions In A Mosaic Trimer Lattice
authors: Xiatao Wang, Li Wang, And Shu Chen
abstract:
