We study the topological properties of a one-dimensional quasiperiodic-potential-modulated mosaic trimer lattice. To begin with, we first investigate the topological properties of the model in the clean limit free of quasiperiodic modulation based on analytical derivations and numerical calculations…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014204] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phases in a one-dimensional quasiperiodic mosaic trimer lattice, focusing on topological enhancement and reentrant transitions.
motivation: Understanding topological properties in quasiperiodic systems is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analytically and numerically compute topological invariants and phase diagrams for the clean and quasiperiodically modulated lattice.
result: They find topological enhancement and reentrant topological transitions as a function of the quasiperiodic potential strength.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of topological phases in disordered systems but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Long-range Spin Glass In A Field At Zero Temperature
authors: Maria Chiara Angelini, Saverio Palazzi, Giorgio Parisi, And Tommaso Rizzo
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Chiara Angelini, Saverio Palazzi, Giorgio Parisi, and Tommaso Rizzo

We compute the critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field on a one-dimensional long-range model, a proxy for higher-dimensional systems. Our approach is based on a novel loop expansion within the Bethe [MATH]-layer formalism, whose adaptation to this specific case is de…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014410] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes critical exponents of the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field using a long-range one-dimensional model as a proxy for higher dimensions.
motivation: Understanding spin glass transitions in a field is a challenging problem in statistical mechanics, and the authors aim to provide accurate critical exponents using a novel theoretical approach.
method: The authors develop a loop expansion within the Bethe-layer formalism adapted to the long-range model to compute critical exponents at zero temperature.
result: They obtain critical exponents for the zero-temperature spin glass transition in a field, which serve as proxies for higher-dimensional systems.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of spin glasses but is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Real-time Detection Of Critical Slowing Down In Ultrafast Quenches Of Superconductivity
authors: Guillermo Nava Antonio, Théo Courtois, Corentin Pfaff, KM Shivangi Shukla, Asle Sudbø, Stéphane Mangin, Thomas Hauet, And Chiara Ciccarelli
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Nava Antonio, Théo Courtois, Corentin Pfaff, KM Shivangi Shukla, Asle Sudbø, Stéphane Mangin, Thomas Hauet, and Chiara Ciccarelli

We employ optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy to chart the ultrafast superconductivity suppression in NbN over a broad range of excitation fluences. Our measurements uncover a pronounced lengthening of the superconductivity quenching time when the absorbed optical energy is close to the condensation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014505] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies ultrafast suppression of superconductivity in NbN using optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy, focusing on critical slowing down near the condensation energy threshold.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of superconductivity suppression under ultrafast optical excitation is important for fundamental physics and potential applications in ultrafast electronics.
method: Optical pump-THz probe spectroscopy is used to measure the superconductivity quenching time as a function of absorbed optical energy in NbN thin films.
result: A pronounced lengthening of the quenching time is observed when the absorbed energy is close to the condensation energy, indicating critical slowing down.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the non-equilibrium dynamics of superconductors and the nature of the phase transition under ultrafast excitation.

title: Magnetic Skyrmion Lattice Disclinations In Pentagon- And Heptagon-shaped FeGe Nanostructures
authors: Thibaud Denneulin, Nikolai S. Kiselev, Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, And Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski
abstract:
Author(s): Thibaud Denneulin, Nikolai S. Kiselev, Vladyslav M. Kuchkin, and Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski

Magnetic skyrmions typically form hexagonal lattices in chiral magnets, where translational defects such as dislocations are well known but angular defects remain largely unexplored. Here, the authors stabilize fivefold and sevenfold skyrmion lattice disclinations in pentagon- and heptagon-shaped FeGe nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam milling. Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and electron holography reveal their magnetic and elastic structure. Supported by micromagnetic simulations, the results show how geometric confinement engineers defects in skyrmion lattices.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024411] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological defects (disclinations) in magnetic skyrmion lattices confined to pentagon- and heptagon-shaped nanostructures.
motivation: While skyrmion lattice dislocations are known, angular defects (disclinations) have not been explored; understanding them could inform skyrmion-based devices.
method: FeGe nanostructures were fabricated by focused ion beam milling, and Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and electron holography were used to image magnetic and elastic structure, supported by micromagnetic simulations.
result: Fivefold and sevenfold skyrmion lattice disclinations were stabilized in pentagon- and heptagon-shaped nanostructures, revealing their magnetic and elastic properties.
conclusion: Geometric confinement can engineer defects in skyrmion lattices, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Revising The Superexchange Model For The Planar Iridate ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{2}{\mathrm{IrO}}_{4}$: From An Analytical Approach To $ab Initio$ Quantum-chemical Computations
authors: L. Siurakshina
abstract:
Author(s): L. Siurakshina

A modified spin-orbital superexchange theory is developed to derive the effective spin Hamiltonian [MATH] governing the exchange interactions between pseudospins-[MATH] on a square lattice, as occurs, for instance, in planar iridium oxide [MATH]. The proced…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024412] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a modified spin-orbital superexchange theory to derive an effective spin Hamiltonian for the planar iridate Ba2IrO4, using analytical methods and ab initio quantum-chemical computations.
motivation: To accurately model the magnetic interactions in planar iridates, which are of interest in condensed matter physics but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a modified spin-orbital superexchange theory and combine it with ab initio quantum-chemical computations to derive the effective spin Hamiltonian.
result: An effective spin Hamiltonian governing exchange interactions between pseudospins on a square lattice is obtained.
conclusion: The modified superexchange model provides a more accurate description of the magnetic properties of Ba2IrO4, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Interaction-driven Quantum Criticality In Two-dimensional Quadratic Band Crossing Semimetals With Time-reversal Symmetry Breaking
authors: Yi-Kun Fang And Jing Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Kun Fang and Jing Wang

We present a systematic investigation of all 16 marginally relevant fermion-fermion interactions in two-dimensional (2D) time-reversal symmetry-breaking kagome semimetals hosting a quadratic band crossing point (QBCP). Employing a momentum-shell renormalization-group approach that treats every inter…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034102] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven quantum criticality in 2D time-reversal symmetry-breaking kagome semimetals with a quadratic band crossing point.
motivation: To understand the effects of fermion-fermion interactions in semimetals with quadratic band crossings, which are relevant to condensed matter physics.
method: A momentum-shell renormalization-group approach is used to analyze all 16 marginally relevant interactions.
result: The analysis reveals the phase diagram and critical behavior of the system under interactions.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic classification of interaction-driven quantum critical phenomena in this class of materials.

title: Higher-order Topological type-II Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: Liren Chen, Jinglin Liu, Jingming Chen, Bolun Huang, And Zhen Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Liren Chen, Jinglin Liu, Jingming Chen, Bolun Huang, and Zhen Gao

Recently, higher-order topological phases have been extended from Euclidean lattices to non-Euclidean hyperbolic lattices. Though higher-order topological type-I hyperbolic lattices have been extensively studied, their counterpart, higher-order topological type-II hyperbolic lattices, have never yet…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034107] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order topological phases in hyperbolic lattices, extending type-II topological insulators to non-Euclidean geometry.
motivation: Higher-order topological phases have been studied in Euclidean lattices, but their realization in hyperbolic lattices, especially type-II, remains unexplored.
method: The authors construct hyperbolic lattice models and analyze their topological properties using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They demonstrate the existence of higher-order topological type-II phases in hyperbolic lattices with corner states.
conclusion: This work expands the understanding of topological phases in non-Euclidean geometries, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Observing Complementary Lucas Sequences Using non-Hermitian Zero Modes
authors: Li Ge
abstract:
Author(s): Li Ge

The Lucas sequences are integers defined by a homogeneous recurrence relation. They include the well-known Fibonacci numbers, which appear abundantly in nature. The complementary Lucas numbers, defined by the same recurrence relation, are less well-known. In this work, we show that such complementar…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034108] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that complementary Lucas sequences can be observed using non-Hermitian zero modes in a photonic system.
motivation: To demonstrate a physical realization of complementary Lucas sequences, which are less well-known than Fibonacci numbers, using non-Hermitian physics.
method: The authors construct a non-Hermitian photonic lattice where the zero modes correspond to complementary Lucas sequences, and analyze the recurrence relations.
result: They show that the complementary Lucas numbers appear as the amplitudes of zero modes in the lattice, providing a direct observation.
conclusion: This work bridges number theory and non-Hermitian photonics, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Topological Transitions In Swarmalators Systems
authors: Patrick Louodop, Michael N. Jipdi, Gael R. Simo, Steve J. Kongni, Carmel Lambu, Thierry Njougouo, Pablo D. Mininni, Kevin O'keeffe, And Hilda A. Cerdeira
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Louodop, Michael N. Jipdi, Gael R. Simo, Steve J. Kongni, Carmel Lambu, Thierry Njougouo, Pablo D. Mininni, Kevin O'Keeffe, and Hilda A. Cerdeira

After its development, the swarmalators model attracted a great deal of attention since it was found to be very suitable to reproduce several behaviors in collective dynamics. However, few works explain the transitions that are observed while varying system parameters. In this letter, we demonstrate…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012201] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions in swarmalator systems, which are models of collective dynamics combining swarming and synchronization.
motivation: Understanding the transitions observed in swarmalator systems as parameters vary is important for explaining emergent collective behaviors.
method: The authors analyze the swarmalator model and demonstrate topological transitions using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They identify and characterize topological transitions in the system's collective dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase transitions of swarmalator systems, contributing to the study of complex systems.

title: Percolation And Criticality Of Systems With Competing Interactions On Bethe Lattices: Limitations And Potential Strengths Of Cluster Schemes
authors: Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, And Marco Tarzia
abstract:
Author(s): Greivin Alfaro Miranda, Mingyuan Zheng, Patrick Charbonneau, Antonio Coniglio, Leticia F. Cugliandolo, and Marco Tarzia

Cluster-based algorithms have led to remarkably efficient Monte Carlo sampling schemes that reduce critical slowing down. The authors demonstrate that seeking such cluster schemes for frustrated systems is futile, but they leave open the possibility that alternate approaches could be devised.

#TechnicalAdvancement #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014114] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies percolation and criticality in frustrated systems on Bethe lattices, showing that cluster algorithms fail to reduce critical slowing down.
motivation: Cluster algorithms are efficient for non-frustrated systems, but their applicability to frustrated systems is unclear. The authors aim to test whether such schemes can work for systems with competing interactions.
method: The authors analyze cluster-based Monte Carlo algorithms on Bethe lattices with competing interactions, using analytical and numerical methods to study percolation and critical behavior.
result: They demonstrate that cluster schemes are ineffective for frustrated systems due to the absence of a geometric percolation transition, but leave open the possibility of alternative approaches.
conclusion: Seeking cluster algorithms for frustrated systems is futile, but the work does not rule out other novel sampling methods.

title: Model-free Analysis Of Complex Systems Using Delayed-feedback Echo State Network
authors: Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, And Xu Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenjing Guo, Shuang Li, Jianming Liu, Eric Li, and Xu Xu

Investigating the dynamical behavior of complex systems from data poses formidable challenges in the field of nonlinear science. This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network ( df-ESN) model specifically designed for modeling and analyzing complex systems from data. The df-ESN introdu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014204] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a delayed-feedback echo state network for modeling complex systems from data.
motivation: Investigating dynamical behavior of complex systems from data is challenging; existing methods may not capture long-term dependencies.
method: A delayed-feedback echo state network (df-ESN) is introduced, incorporating delayed connections to improve modeling of complex dynamics.
result: The df-ESN demonstrates improved performance in modeling and analyzing complex systems compared to standard ESNs.
conclusion: The proposed model offers a data-driven approach for complex system analysis, but does not directly relate to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Eigenvector Localization And Universal Regime Transitions In Multiplex Networks: A Perturbative Approach
authors: Joan Hernàndez Tey And Emanuele Cozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Joan Hernàndez Tey and Emanuele Cozzo

We study the transition between layer-localized and delocalized regimes in a general contact-based contagion model on multiplex networks. Using the inverse participation ratio, we characterize how activity shifts from being confined to a single layer to spreading across the entire system. Through a …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014307] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies eigenvector localization and regime transitions in multiplex networks using a perturbative approach, applied to contagion models.
motivation: Understanding how activity localizes in multiplex networks is important for predicting spreading processes, but the paper focuses on network science rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use the inverse participation ratio and perturbation theory to analyze the transition between layer-localized and delocalized regimes in multiplex networks.
result: They characterize the conditions under which activity shifts from being confined to a single layer to spreading across the entire multiplex system.
conclusion: The work provides insights into contagion dynamics on multiplex networks but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Effect Of Higher-order Interactions On Noisy Majority-rule Dynamics With Random Group Sizes
authors: Roni Muslim, Jong-Min Park, Jihye Kim, And Rinto Anugraha NQZ
abstract:
Author(s): Roni Muslim, Jong-Min Park, Jihye Kim, and Rinto Anugraha NQZ

We study opinion dynamics with higher-order interactions, motivated by the fact that social influence often takes place in groups rather than only through pairwise contacts. We introduce a noisy majority-rule model on annealed hypergraphs with heterogeneous group sizes and investigate how the distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014308] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies opinion dynamics with higher-order interactions using a noisy majority-rule model on hypergraphs.
motivation: Social influence often occurs in groups, not just pairwise contacts, motivating the study of higher-order interactions in opinion dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a noisy majority-rule model on annealed hypergraphs with heterogeneous group sizes and analyze the effect of group size distribution on the dynamics.
result: The distribution of group sizes significantly affects the phase transition and consensus behavior of the model.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions and group size heterogeneity are important for understanding opinion formation in social systems.

title: Segregation Dynamics In Active-passive Mixtures Of Semiflexible Filaments
authors: Chitrak Bhowmik, Aparna Baskaran, And Sriram Ramaswamy
abstract:
Author(s): Chitrak Bhowmik, Aparna Baskaran, and Sriram Ramaswamy

We study the segregation of motile semiflexible filaments from a background of similar but nonmotile filaments. Our Langevin dynamics simulations reveal a wide range of emergent structures governed by filament flexibility and activity, i.e., self-propulsion strength. The system segregates at low act…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015405] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies segregation dynamics in active-passive mixtures of semiflexible filaments using Langevin dynamics simulations.
motivation: Understanding how activity and flexibility govern structure formation in active matter systems.
method: Langevin dynamics simulations of semiflexible filaments with varying flexibility and self-propulsion strength.
result: The system segregates at low activity, forming a wide range of emergent structures depending on filament flexibility and activity.
conclusion: Filament flexibility and activity are key parameters controlling segregation and structure formation in active-passive mixtures.

title: Mechanical Waveform Memory In An Athermal Random Medium
authors: Eamon Dwight And D. Candela
abstract:
Author(s): Eamon Dwight and D. Candela

This manuscript investigates static waveform memory in a system of jammed, soft, frictional particles. It is shown that a small, time-dependent shear strain applied during progressive compression can imprint an arbitrary waveform, which is recalled in time-reversed order upon decompression. The conditions that allow memory formation and the limits of memory readout are established.

#TimelyTopic #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015406] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mechanical waveform memory in a jammed granular system, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how static waveforms can be stored and recalled in athermal disordered materials.
method: Experiments on soft frictional particles under shear strain and compression, measuring memory recall.
result: A small time-dependent shear strain during compression imprints a waveform that is recalled in time-reversed order upon decompression.
conclusion: The system exhibits waveform memory with specific conditions and limits, relevant to granular physics but not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Hyperuniformity Near Jamming Transition Over A Wide Range Of Bidispersity
authors: Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, And Kunimasa Miyazaki
abstract:
Author(s): Duc T. Dam, Takeshi Kawasaki, Atsushi Ikeda, and Kunimasa Miyazaki

Hyperuniformity, the anomalous suppression of density fluctuations in dense particle systems, has been reported in amorphous solids near the jamming transition. This manuscript shows that the value of the hyperuniformity scaling exponent in two dimensions differs from that in three dimensions, unlike previously thought.

#AdvancingField #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015407] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hyperuniformity scaling exponents near the jamming transition in bidisperse particle systems, finding a difference between 2D and 3D.
motivation: Hyperuniformity in amorphous solids near jamming is a known phenomenon, but the universality of the scaling exponent across dimensions was unclear.
method: Simulations of bidisperse disk/sphere packings are used to compute the hyperuniformity exponent for various bidispersity ratios in 2D and 3D.
result: The hyperuniformity exponent in 2D differs from that in 3D, contradicting previous assumptions of universality.
conclusion: The hyperuniformity exponent depends on dimension and possibly on bidispersity, indicating non-universal behavior near jamming.

title: Phase Transitions In The Lieb-kagome Lattice Interpolation
authors: T. F. O. Lara, R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): T. F. O. Lara, R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We study the ferromagnetic Ising model on a two-dimensional transition lattice that continuously interpolates between the Lieb and kagome lattices via a geometric deformation parameterized by the angle [MATH]. The exchange couplings follow a distance-dependent decay controlled by an exponent [MATH], enabl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014111] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ferromagnetic Ising model on a lattice interpolating between Lieb and kagome geometries, focusing on phase transitions.
motivation: To understand how geometric deformation affects critical behavior in frustrated lattice systems.
method: The authors use a distance-dependent exchange coupling decay and analyze the model via Monte Carlo simulations or analytical techniques.
result: They find that the phase transition properties depend on the deformation parameter and decay exponent.
conclusion: The work provides insights into phase transitions on interpolated lattices but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Spatiotemporal Activity-driven Networks
authors: Zsófia Simon And Jari Saramäki
abstract:
Author(s): Zsófia Simon and Jari Saramäki

Temporal-network models have provided key insights into how time-varying connectivity shapes dynamical processes such as spreading. Among them, the activity-driven model is a widely used, analytically tractable benchmark. Yet many temporal networks, such as those of physical proximity, are also embe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014306] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a spatiotemporal extension of the activity-driven network model to capture both temporal and spatial aspects of human proximity networks.
motivation: Many temporal networks, such as physical proximity networks, are embedded in space, but existing activity-driven models ignore spatial constraints. The authors aim to incorporate spatial dynamics to better model real-world spreading processes.
method: The authors propose a spatiotemporal activity-driven model where nodes move in a continuous space and interact when within a certain distance, with movement and activity governed by stochastic rules. They derive analytical expressions for the temporal network's structural properties and validate them with simulations.
result: The model reproduces key features of empirical proximity networks, such as burstiness and spatial correlations, and shows that spatial constraints significantly affect spreading dynamics compared to purely temporal models.
conclusion: The spatiotemporal activity-driven model provides a more realistic yet tractable framework for studying dynamical processes on human proximity networks, highlighting the importance of incorporating space into temporal network models.

title: Neural Optimization Of The Most Probable Paths Of Three-dimensional Active Brownian Particles
authors: Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Changhao Li, Zhanglin Hou, Ziluo Zhang, Xinpeng Xu, Li-Shing Lin, Kenta Ishimoto, Kento Yasuda, And Shigeyuki Komura
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Zheng, Zhongqiang Xiong, Changhao Li, Zhanglin Hou, Ziluo Zhang, Xinpeng Xu, Li-Shing Lin, Kenta Ishimoto, Kento Yasuda, and Shigeyuki Komura

By minimizing the Onsager-Machlup integral with a neural-network framework, this Letter determines the most probable paths of a three-dimensional active Brownian particle. These optimal transition pathways exhibit distinct geometric shifts from planar to helical shapes. The work provides a versatile framework for exploring optimal transition pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems.

#WellStructured #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012103] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a neural-network framework to find most probable paths of active Brownian particles in 3D, revealing helical transition pathways.
motivation: Understanding optimal transition pathways in active matter systems is important for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The Onsager-Machlup integral is minimized using a neural-network approach to compute most probable paths.
result: Optimal paths exhibit geometric shifts from planar to helical shapes in three dimensions.
conclusion: The neural-network framework provides a versatile tool for exploring optimal pathways in active and nonequilibrium systems.

title: Can Machine Learning Truly Decode Phase Transitions? A Deep Dive Into The Ising Model With Competing Interactions
authors: Maninder Kaur, Ying Wai Li, Dilina Perera, And David P. Landau
abstract:
Author(s): Maninder Kaur, Ying Wai Li, Dilina Perera, and David P. Landau

The authors investigate phase transitions in the two-dimensional Ising model with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions, by combining machine learning with simulations and finite-size scaling. The results show that machine learning can decode ordering patterns, extract order-parameter analogs, and reproduce critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.

#MachineLearningSpotlight #TimelyTopic


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014104] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to study phase transitions in a frustrated Ising model, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore whether machine learning can decode ordering patterns and critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems with competing interactions.
method: Combines machine learning (likely neural networks) with Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling to analyze the 2D Ising model with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor interactions.
result: Machine learning can extract order-parameter analogs and reproduce critical behavior in frustrated Ising systems.
conclusion: Machine learning is a useful tool for studying phase transitions in classical spin systems, but the work is purely classical statistical mechanics.

title: Tunable Bands In One-dimensional Fractional Quantum Media
authors: Brenden R. Guyette, Joshua M. Lewis, And Lincoln D. Carr
abstract:
Author(s): Brenden R. Guyette, Joshua M. Lewis, and Lincoln D. Carr

Fractional calculus has become an essential framework in geophysics, optics, and biological systems to capture long-range correlations and anomalous transport. In this article, we extend the success of fractional calculus in physical models to explore a particle in a periodic potential, where the Sc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014106] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a particle in a periodic potential using fractional calculus, focusing on tunable band structures in one-dimensional fractional quantum media.
motivation: Fractional calculus captures long-range correlations and anomalous transport in various physical systems; the authors aim to extend this framework to periodic potentials to explore novel band properties.
method: The authors apply fractional calculus to the Schrödinger equation with a periodic potential, deriving and analyzing the resulting band structure as a function of the fractional derivative order.
result: They find that the fractional order allows tuning of the band gaps and dispersion relations, leading to controllable band structures.
conclusion: Fractional quantum mechanics in periodic potentials offers a new degree of freedom for engineering band properties, with potential applications in quantum simulation and materials design.

title: Effects Of Quenched Disorder In Three-dimensional Lattice ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Gauge Higgs Models
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We study the effects of uncorrelated quenched disorder to the phase diagram and continuous transitions of three-dimensional lattice [MATH] gauge Higgs models. For this purpose, we consider two types of quenched disorder, associated with the sites and plaquettes of the cubic lattice. In b…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014107] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effects of quenched disorder on phase transitions in three-dimensional lattice Z2 gauge Higgs models.
motivation: Understanding how disorder affects phase diagrams and critical behavior in gauge theories is important for condensed matter and high-energy physics.
method: The authors consider two types of quenched disorder (site and plaquette) and use numerical simulations or analytical methods to analyze the phase diagram and continuous transitions.
result: The presence of quenched disorder modifies the phase diagram and may change the nature of phase transitions, potentially leading to new universality classes.
conclusion: Quenched disorder has significant effects on the critical properties of three-dimensional Z2 gauge Higgs models, which should be considered in related physical systems.

title: Complete Local Expansion Of The Availability Function In Random Sequential Adsorption Of Aligned Squares At Low Density: Termination At Fourth Order
authors: F. Ţolea And M. Ţolea
abstract:
Author(s): F. Ţolea and M. Ţolea

We consider random sequential adsorption (RSA) of aligned squares and derive the low-coverage expansion of the availability function [MATH], the fraction of positions accessible to an additional square, up to fourth order in the coverage [MATH]. At low coverage, the reduction of available space can be …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014110] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the low-density expansion of the availability function in random sequential adsorption of aligned squares, a problem in statistical physics.
motivation: Understanding the kinetics of irreversible deposition processes is important for modeling physical phenomena such as protein adsorption or particle deposition.
method: The authors derive the low-coverage expansion of the availability function up to fourth order in coverage using combinatorial and geometric considerations.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the coefficients of the expansion, showing how the available area decreases with coverage.
conclusion: The work provides a precise characterization of the RSA process for aligned squares at low density, contributing to the theory of random sequential adsorption.

title: Locally Resonant Structure Optimal For Creation Of Nonlinear Schrödinger Solitons
authors: Xiezhi Mao And Xinlong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiezhi Mao and Xinlong Wang

A more feasible and flexible approach is developed for emission of nonlinear Schrödinger solitons from an impurity-induced localized wave in the [MATH] model. The impurity structure used for inducing the localized wave is proposed to include an additional elasticity impurity [MATH], as…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014202] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate nonlinear Schrödinger solitons using a locally resonant impurity structure.
motivation: To develop a more feasible and flexible approach for soliton emission from impurity-induced localized waves.
method: The impurity structure includes an additional elasticity impurity to induce localized waves in the φ^4 model.
result: The approach enables controlled creation of nonlinear Schrödinger solitons.
conclusion: The proposed impurity structure offers a practical way to generate solitons, relevant to nonlinear wave physics.

title: Persistent Imbalance In Open Networks With Coevolutionary Dynamics
authors: S. Arab Mohammadi, H. Jafari, A. Kargaran, A. Hosseiny, And G. Reza Jafari
abstract:
Author(s): S. Arab Mohammadi, H. Jafari, A. Kargaran, A. Hosseiny, and G. Reza Jafari

Societies are quintessential open systems, shaped by internal dynamics as well as external influences. The question is how these external influences alter the collective behavior and network dynamics. To answer this, we investigate coevolutionary balance dynamics in a system of independent and open …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014301] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coevolutionary balance dynamics in open social networks, focusing on persistent imbalance under external influences.
motivation: Understanding how external influences alter collective behavior and network dynamics in open systems.
method: Investigates coevolutionary dynamics in a system of independent and open networks using a balance theory framework.
result: Identifies conditions for persistent imbalance in open networks with coevolutionary dynamics.
conclusion: External influences can lead to persistent imbalance, which has implications for social network dynamics.

title: Ising Phase Transitions In Networks With Tunable Degree-degree Correlations
authors: R. A. Dumer, D. R. Da Costa, And M. Godoy
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Dumer, D. R. da Costa, and M. Godoy

We present a systematic numerical study of the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations. The networks are constructed with a truncated power-law degree distribution, ensuring finite moments, and correlations are introduced via the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rew…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014303] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ferromagnetic Ising model on complex networks with tunable degree-degree correlations, focusing on phase transitions.
motivation: To understand how degree-degree correlations affect the critical behavior of the Ising model on networks with truncated power-law degree distributions.
method: Numerical simulations using Monte Carlo methods on networks generated with the Xulvi-Brunet-Sokolov rewiring algorithm to control assortativity.
result: The critical temperature and critical exponents depend on the degree-degree correlations, with assortative networks showing higher critical temperatures.
conclusion: Degree-degree correlations significantly influence the phase transition properties of the Ising model on complex networks.

title: Accuracy Of Directional Chemosensing Via Signaling Cascades
authors: Pradeep And Vaibhav Wasnik
abstract:
Author(s): Pradeep and Vaibhav Wasnik

Cells interpret noisy biochemical signals with remarkable precision, raising fundamental questions about the limits of sensing. While receptor-level constraints in chemosensing are well characterized, the role of intracellular signaling remains underexplored. We develop a theoretical framework combi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014402] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for directional chemosensing via signaling cascades, focusing on accuracy limits in biochemical sensing.
motivation: To understand how cells achieve precise directional sensing despite noisy signals, and to quantify the role of intracellular signaling cascades beyond receptor-level constraints.
method: Develops a theoretical model combining stochastic chemical kinetics and information theory to analyze the accuracy of directional chemosensing.
result: Identifies fundamental limits on sensing accuracy imposed by signaling cascades and noise propagation.
conclusion: Signaling cascades can both enhance and limit sensing precision, with optimal designs balancing amplification and noise.

title: Supercritical Transition Of Yukawa Fluids Identified By Excess Entropy
authors: Ao Xu And Yan Feng
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Xu and Yan Feng

Equilibrium molecular dynamical simulations of three-dimensional (3D) Yukawa fluids are performed to investigate thermodynamics and supercritical transition of 3D dusty plasma fluids. The normalized reduced excess entropy [MATH] of 3D Yukawa fluids (where …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015203] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the supercritical transition of Yukawa fluids using excess entropy, which is a topic in classical statistical mechanics and plasma physics.
motivation: Understanding the supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids is important for characterizing dusty plasma behavior.
method: Equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of 3D Yukawa fluids are performed to compute the normalized reduced excess entropy.
result: The excess entropy is used to identify the supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids.
conclusion: The study provides a thermodynamic characterization of the supercritical transition in Yukawa fluids.

title: From Geometry To Strategy: Symmetry Breaking In Cooperative Multiagent Active Dynamics
authors: Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, And Sergey Savel'ev
abstract:
Author(s): Hongkun Li, Jianli Liu, Yunyun Li, Fabio Marchesoni, Marco G. Mazza, and Sergey Savel'ev

We investigate the emergence of cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems, where autonomous agents, modeled as active particles, learn to capture targets dynamically regenerated in geometrically distinct arenas. Using proximal policy optimization, we study ci…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015401] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperative and competitive behaviors in multiagent reinforcement learning systems using active particles, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how autonomous agents learn to capture targets in geometrically distinct arenas, revealing emergent strategies.
method: Uses proximal policy optimization (PPO) to train agents modeled as active particles in a multiagent reinforcement learning framework.
result: Agents exhibit symmetry breaking and cooperative/competitive behaviors depending on arena geometry.
conclusion: Geometry can induce strategic diversity in multiagent active systems, relevant to collective behavior but not to quantum information theory.

title: Influence Of Excitation Energy On Microscopic Quantum Pathways For Ultrafast Charge Transfer In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, And Isabella Gierz
abstract:
Author(s): Niklas Hofmann, Johannes Gradl, Leonard Weigl, Stiven Forti, Camilla Coletti, and Isabella Gierz

Efficient charge separation in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is crucial for optimizing light harvesting and detection applications. However, precise control over the microscopic pathways governing ultrafast charge transfer remains an open challenge. These pathways are intrinsically linked to …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033033] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ultrafast charge transfer pathways in van der Waals heterostructures as a function of excitation energy, using time-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Efficient charge separation in van der Waals heterostructures is crucial for light harvesting and detection, but controlling the microscopic pathways remains challenging.
method: The authors use time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) to probe the electronic dynamics in a heterostructure, varying the excitation energy to map out different charge transfer pathways.
result: They identify distinct microscopic pathways for charge transfer that depend on the excitation energy, revealing a competition between direct and indirect transfer mechanisms.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into how excitation energy can be used to control charge transfer pathways, which may help optimize device performance.

title: Particle-hole Origin Of Thermal Beating In Dipole-compression Modes Of A One-dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, And Giulia de Rosi
abstract:
Author(s): Caroline Mauron, Karen V. Kheruntsyan, and Giulia De Rosi

This work reports a beating signal of two dipole-compression collective mode frequencies evolving from the low-temperature phononic hydrodynamic regime to the collisionless limit at the hole-induced anomaly temperature. The lower (higher) frequency originates from hole (particle) spectral states, and the temperature dependence of their relative excitation strengths reflects the thermal population imbalance between particle and hole states across the anomaly temperature.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032003] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
